steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch pan.

Stir flour, 1 cup sugar, and baking powder together in a medium bowl; mix in salt and cinnamon, if desired. Use a fork or pastry cutter to blend in butter and egg. Dough will be crumbly. Pat half of dough into the prepared pan.
Stir 1/2 cup sugar and cornstarch together in another bowl; gently mix in blueberries. Sprinkle blueberry mixture evenly over prepared crust. Crumble remaining dough over berry layer.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is slightly brown, about 45 minutes. Cool completely before cutting into squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Blueberry Crumb Bars
raw_recipe.description: These blueberry bars have a buttery crust, a delicious fresh blueberry filling, and a cinnamon crumble topping for a delicious summer treat.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make simple blueberry crumb bars. These easy bar cookies feature a simple crust bottom topped with blueberries and a cinnamon crumble. Use any of your favorite berries with this versatile recipe.

review.reviewBody: I'VE MADE 4 PANS OF THESE IN JUST ONE WEEK. FIRST PAN FOR HOME TRIAL USING JUST WHITE SUGAR.....VERY GOOD. NEXT THREE PANS (ONE FOR A COOKOUT, ONE FOR A GRADUATION PARTY & ONE TO GO TO W/MY SON TO N.HAMPSHIRE FOR A NASCAR RACE) I USED 1/2 C. WHITE SUGAR & 1/2 C. LIGHT BROWN SUGAR FOR CRUST....EVEN BETTER. ALSO ADDED 1 TSP. VANILLA EXTRACT TO BEATEN EGG. I'LL BE MAKING THEM AGAIN THIS WEEK FOR MY BEST FRIEND'S BIRTHDAY. THEY DO TRAVEL EXTREMELY WELL. SINCE I LIVE IN NEW ENGLAND, I'VE TAKEN ADVANTAGE OF THE FRESH BLUEBERRIES THAT ARE AT THEIR PEAK.

Really yummy! I used butter instead of shortening, and used frozen berries. I cut the recipe in half too, and used part whole-wheat pastry flour. I did the "dough" in my food processor, and it never really came together, it was just a powdery mixture. I thought it wouldn't work, but went ahead with it anyways and it all came together during baking. These turned out really well. For those of you that said the dough part didn't have any real flavor, it's probably due to the shortening. Shortening has no real flavor (plus it's yucky and bad for you). Try butter, it's so much better!

I can't begin to say how great this recipe is! My sister told me it was good, so I decided to give it a try. Boy, was she right! It is crumbly, but I just added a little liquid (water mixed with lemon juice and vanilla for extra flavor) to the half of crumbs used for the base, and pre-cooked it for about 5 minutes. The base was not nearly as crumbly as the top this way. FYI, I used frozen berries for this, without defrosting first, and it baked up perfectly in the same amount of time.

ETA that I have only ever used butter with this recipe- I do not cook with shortening. I also use at least half whole wheat flour. Healthier and tastier!

This was amazing, especially warmed up with vanilla bean ice cream! I will make this over and over again! I took some tips from the other reviewers and added 1/2c sugar + 1/2c brown sugar to the crust, along with quite a bit more cinnamon then called for, nutmeg and orange zest seasoning. I used butter rather than shortening. I added vanilla to the egg mixture, and a teaspoon more cornstarch to the blueberries; I didn't want them to be at all runny! I squeezed lemon on top of the berries, sprinkled a bit more orange zest, and then used my hands to sprinkle the crust on top. Squishing the little butter clumps with my hands made for a really great crispy topping. I ended up baking for 57 mins total, only because I used my timer in 6 min increments after the 45 min original timer. It probably could've gone the whole hour..
 
I used an 11x7 glass dish (2 qts) because I wanted thicker bars, and lined it with butter sprayed foil instead of greasing the pan. After it cooled, I drizzled a lemon/vanilla glaze I made by using powdered sugar, water, and lemon and vanilla extracts. It turned out SO well, the crust was buttery and crunchy with a hint of cinnamon.. the blueberries were sweet and held wonderfully with the extra cornstarch, and the lemon vanilla glaze? Perfection!!

Wow! This was great! I followed others' advice and used 1/2 cup white and 1/2 cup light brown sugar along with salted butter and 1 teaspoon cinnamon for the crust. I mixed up half the dough in the food processor, which gave it a cookie dough consistency -perfect for spreading in the bottom of the pan for the crust. I used an extra cup of frozen berries, although next time I think I'd double the berries. I still used only 1/2 cup white sugar for the berries, but doubled the cornstarch to 2 Tablespoons. The crumb topping I assembled by cutting the butter in with a pastry harp. A definite keeper!

Excellent recipe. I have made this many times and over time have adjusted the recipe to suit my family’s tastes. I use butter instead of shortening. I add a teaspoon of vanilla and 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon to crumble. I mix the crumble in my Kitchenaid stand mixer. I firmly pressed the bottom layer of crumble in the pan to make a nice crust. When I use frozen blueberries I increase the cooking time by 10 minutes. These always turn out great.

Very good! Used an 8 X 8 inch pan and reduced all of the ingredients by half except for the egg and cornstarch; used a pinch of salt and a 1/4 tsp. of cinnamon. Substituted softened butter for the shortening; brown sugar for 1/2 of the sugar for the dough; and rolled oats for 1/3 of the flour. Added 1/2 tsp. vanilla and the zest of 1/2 lemon to the dough mixture; added the juice of 1/2 lemon to the berries along with an extra 2 Tbs. of sugar to the berries. Next time will add a total of an extra 3 Tbs. of sugar to the berries. Like my berries more sweet than tart. Used 1 cup each of fresh blueberries and blackberries because that's what I had on hand. Came out perfect; not too sweet or tart. Reduced oven temperature to 350 degrees because I used a glass pan and baked 45 minutes. Yum! Considered topping with some powdered sugar but it didn't need it. Didn't have any ice cream so ate plain right out of the pan. Will try with some whipped cream next. Will definitely make again. 5/4/17 update: Made again today with raspberries and an extra 3 Tbs. of sugar. Good, but not the masterpiece the blueberry/blackberry combo was. They were out of this world.

I made 2 pans of this in 2 days. 1st time I made it, I thought the bars were a bit thin and slightly dry. 2nd time, I cut the entire recipe in half but added 2 additional cups of berries (fresh blueberries, raspberries, blackberries). I used brown sugar in the crust instead of white sugar and used butter instead of shortening. Put it in 8x8 pan and cooked 35 minutes. It was perfect and the additional fruit made it so moist. Topped with a homemade whipped topping. My friends raved over it.

To make these less bland: use half white/brown sugar, butter (no question!), 1-2 tsp salt, 2 tsp almond (not vanilla) extract whisked with egg before adding, 4 tsp cornstarch & add 1 cup slivered almonds just to the topping. Raspberries & half white/whole wheat flour would also be good substitutions. As with all bars, a light cooking spray & parchment lining the pan, plus refrigerating overnight, make cutting a breeze.

Made a ton of blueberry jam and wanted a good recipe to pair with it. This is it. Instead of fresh blueberries I used my jam with some corn starch. I baked the base layer for 5 minutes and then added the jam, about two cups. Covered with second half of dough and continued baking 40 minutes. Wonderful.

This is a really great recipe, I made a few changes I first cut the recipe in half and then I did what others suggested and changed the shortening for butter (becel margarine lol). I also used 2/3 of the crumble to the bottom crust and then mixed roughly another 1/4 cup of butter, 1/3 brown sugar ,1/3 of rolled oats to the left over crumble, as for the blueberries I added a table spoon of corn starch, 2 1/2 cups blueberries, 1/2 cup sugar and half of a lemon juiced in.

I used 1/2 c. White flour and 1/2 c. brown sugar for the crust. I also whisked 1-2 tsp vanilla paste into the egg. I used several dashes of cinnamon and no salt because I used salted Irish butter. I probably used closer to 4.5 c. of fresh blueberries. It was a huge hit at a picnic I took it to.

Fantastic recipe. Very easy to follow and only made a few minor tweaks. Used 1/2 white sugar and 1/2 brown sugar as many reviewers suggested. Also used butter flavored shortening cause I was making it for someone with a dairy allergy. Used frozen mixed berries (raspberries, blackberries, and blueberries). Turned out amazing.
I added lemon zest and juice to the dough mix. It really gave it pizzazz

Made these for a luncheon at our house for our pastor and family of 8. They were gone and everyone loved them. I made them as written, except I added a splash of vanilla extract which helped with the crumbly dough. I baked that for 5 minutes, too. I am going to make them again tomorrow for another visiting family, and I’ll try the suggestion of doing half granulated and half brown sugars for the crust. I’m going to cut the bars a little smaller than 15 in the pan as we had several little kids and they only ate half their bars. So delicious and hearty!
Easy to make and good balance of flavors
This recipe is really easy and delicious. Highly Recommend

This is do good, I made this a few times with different berries and fruits instead of blueberries I used strawberries and rhubarbe (no cinnamon). I also made it with apples (with cinnamon). It was excellent each time.
Followed recipe exactly. This was super simple to make, flavors are amazing. My family LOVED it! Could easily swap blueberries for other fruit.

I had to freeze half of it because my husband pretty much ate the other half to himself! I did add some vanilla to the egg and extra cornstarch to firm up the filling. I’m making another tray tomorrow.
